gap_text: Retrieval of dated financial sources is not established. The Qdrant/SocratiCode receipts record no financial-document corpus.
next_check: Index a dated corpus of FOMC statements from federalreserve.gov into a disposable Qdrant collection and run dated queries with gold answers, recording recall and date correctness.

preregistration.expectation: Dense retrieval over FOMC statements (federalreserve.gov, 2023-2026) finds the right meeting for many dated queries, but pure semantic similarity will often return a neighbouring meeting because statements are nearly identical; a payload date filter derived from the query should raise date correctness to ~100%.
criteria: Download the FOMC calendar page and every linked 2023-01..latest statement HTML (disclosed network download, small); record URLs, sha256 and fetched_at.

Generate queries mechanically from the corpus before any retrieval: for each statement, one dated query naming the meeting month and year and asking for the federal funds target range decided; gold = that statement's date and the target range regex-extracted from its text. Seal the query file (sha256) before indexing.

Index into a disposable Qdrant 1.19.1 collection on 127.0.0.1:27333 with payload {date,url}; embeddings from the same Nemotron-3-Embed-1B endpoint the adopted SocratiCode profile uses (read-only /v1/embeddings calls).
Report recall@1/@3/@5 of the gold document and top-1 date correctness for arm dense and arm dense+date-filter; report answer correctness (top-1 document's extracted target range equals gold).
No query rewriting after scores are seen.

late_amendment.label: late preregistration: written AFTER the first run's results (both arms 30/30) were seen
late_amendment.expectation: With the dateline and any explicit full dates (Month DD, YYYY) removed from the indexed text, the dense arm's top-1 date correctness drops well below 1.0 (neighbouring meetings with similar wording), while the dense+date_filter arm stays at 1.0 because the date lives in the payload.
criteria: Same 30 sealed queries, same embedding endpoint, new collection g2amw_fomc_statements_nodate.
Remove every 'Month DD, YYYY' pattern and the 'For release at ... Share' header from the text before embedding; payload dates unchanged.
Report the same metrics for both arms; no further changes after seeing scores.

results.queries: 30 dated queries 'What target range for the federal funds rate did the FOMC set at its <Month> <YYYY> meeting?', gold = that statement's date and regex-extracted target range (8 distinct ranges)
results.reading: Dense retrieval found the right meeting only because each statement carries its own dateline; with datelines removed it returned the wrong meeting 28/30 times (mostly 2026-01-28). Date correctness for dated financial sources therefore needs an as-of payload filter; with it, 30/30 in both conditions. The preregistered expectation (neighbouring-meeting confusion without a filter) was refuted for the as-published text and confirmed only after ablation.

limits: One source type (FOMC statements), 30 templated queries; not a holdout of analyst questions or a broad financial RAG benchmark.
'Answer correctness' is a regex lookup of the retrieved document's target range, not a model-generated answer.
Queried through Qdrant directly with the adopted embedder, not through SocratiCode's code-oriented tools (SocratiCode exposes no date payload filter).
Network downloads from federalreserve.gov (about 2.8 MB total) are disclosed; raw HTML stays in the cache, hashes are committed.
